notes.meaning: God's people are called to offer a fresh song of praise to the Lord for His continuing mercies. True worship belongs in the gathered assembly of the godly, where believers unite their voices. Praise is the natural and joyous response whenever God works in new ways to deliver His people.

The people of Israel are urged to rejoice in God as their Maker, who not only created them but formed them into His own special nation. They are also to celebrate Him as their true King who lovingly rules and protects them. Gladly submitting to His authority brings true joy to His followers.

Worship in ancient Israel involved the whole person, using dancing, tambourines, and harps to celebrate God's goodness. These joyful sounds and movements gave expression to the overflowing happiness of a thankful heart.

differ.view: Some hold that Old Testament dancing and musical instruments were temporary ceremonial shadows, so Christian worship today should focus simply on singing with the heart and understanding.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: The Hebrew word usually translated as dancing may instead refer to a wind instrument, such as a pipe or flute, played alongside the tambourine and harp.

notes.meaning: The Lord does not look down on His people with indifference; He takes deep pleasure in them. He lifts up the humble and oppressed, clothing them with the beauty of His salvation and deliverance.
God's faithful servants can exult in the honor He has granted them. Even at night upon their beds, when everything is quiet, their hearts and voices are full of peaceful songs of praise to Him.

The worshippers are pictured with the high praises of God in their mouths and a double-edged sword in their hands. While ancient Israel fought literal battles in God's service, for believers today this points to combining heartfelt worship with the Word of God in spiritual warfare.

differ.view: High praise is seen as an active weapon of spiritual warfare that works alongside the word of God to break demonic strongholds.

notes.meaning: Ancient Israel was appointed by God to carry out His righteous judgment on corrupt and hostile nations. This was not an act of personal revenge or human anger, but the execution of God's holy justice against evil.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: These verses may reflect the historical battles of the Maccabean period, when Jewish fighters went out against their Syrian oppressors while praying and chanting praises to God.

notes.meaning: Even powerful kings and proud nobles who opposed God were taken captive and bound in iron chains. This demonstrated that no earthly ruler or army can withstand the power of the Lord when He defends His people.

These victories carried out the judgments that God had already recorded in His holy word. Sharing in the triumph of God's justice is a great honor belonging to all His godly people, ending the psalm with another joyful call to praise the Lord.
